title: Neural tissue mapping resolves pancreatic cancer spectral differences
summary: Convolutional networks assigned Raman spectra to cellular regions in pancreatic tumor tissue from 15 patients. Region-specific analysis suggested different nuclear protein structures in conventional ductal cancer and intraductal papillary mucinous carcinoma, helping separate signals obscured in whole-tissue measurements. These are exploratory spectroscopic interpretations, without direct confirmation of particular protein identities, causal mechanisms or patient-level diagnostic accuracy.
ai_technology: One-dimensional convolutional neural network; shallow neural network
organization: Jagiellonian University; University Hospital Krakow; AGH University of Krakow

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: New tissue Raman measurements from 16 slides representing 15 patients, learned subcellular spectrum assignment, and region-specific spectral comparisons.
evidence.unknown: Independent biological confirmation and clinical diagnostic utility remain unestablished; internal spectrum-level splitting and augmentation do not establish independent patient-level performance.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN assigns spectra to tumor-type-specific nuclear and cytoplasmic regions, enabling subsequent region-specific interpretation of measured Raman bands.
